answers.stem_only: Status page: switch its GetItem calls to eventually consistent reads, which cost half the read capacity of strongly consistent reads and fit data a few seconds old. Nightly report: a filter expression is applied after the read, so the Scan still consumes capacity for the whole table; use a sparse global secondary index on an attribute that only open orders carry and query the index (its reads use the index capacity, not the table's).

Optimistic locking: add a version number attribute, increment it on each save, and make PutItem conditional (condition expression) on the version that was read; a failed condition (ConditionalCheckFailedException) tells the second agent to reload. A plain conditional write costs normal write units, whereas a transaction costs twice as much and BatchWriteItem has no conditions.
